title: Fix fallback parameter warning spam in controller manager by ktgilliam · Pull Request #3270 · ros-controls/ros2_control · GitHub
body_rendered_text:
Description


In ControllerManager::load_controller(), fallback_controllers and

node_options_args are declared using the type-only overload of

declare_parameter():



```
declare_parameter(fallback_ctrl_param, rclcpp::ParameterType::PARAMETER_STRING_ARRAY);
```



This leaves the parameter declared but uninitialized... its type is known to

rclcpp but it has no value. Any external caller that subsequently invokes the CM

node's /get_parameters service for these keys (e.g. rqt_controller_manager,

foxglove_bridge, ros2 param get, etc) triggers a

ParameterUninitializedException inside rclcpp's ParameterService handler,

which logs it as:



```
[WARN] [rclcpp]: Failed to get parameters: parameter '<controller_name>.fallback_controllers' is not initialized

```



Because tools like rqt_controller_manager poll the CM periodically, this

warning repeats continuously for every loaded controller.


The fix is to supply an empty default value instead of a bare type, making the

parameter queryable immediately after declaration:



```
declare_parameter(fallback_ctrl_param, std::vector<std::string>{});
declare_parameter(node_options_args_param, std::vector<std::string>{});
```



Fixes # (issue) (Didn't create an issue).


Is this user-facing behavior change?


Yes. Users will no longer see repeated [WARN] [rclcpp]: Failed to get parameters: parameter '<name>.fallback_controllers' is not initialized messages

in the ros2_control_node output when any ROS 2 tool queries the controller

manager's parameters.


Did you use Generative AI?


I had help from copilot diagnosing the issue, but the two changed lines are mine.


Additional Information


The same ParameterUninitializedException path in rclcpp's ParameterService

is triggered by node_options_args for the same reason; both are fixed in this

PR. The fix does not change any observable behavior for controllers that do or do

not configure fallback controllers.
